concerns.text: Phase 0 tasks (e.g., T008, T010, T011, T012, T013, T014) declare dependencies on foundational tasks T005, T006, T007 that are defined later in Phase 2, violating the FR‑010 “foundational‑tasks‑first” rule.
Task T010 depends on T006, but T006 (unit‑normalization utility) is created in Phase 2, i.e., after Phase 0, breaking producer‑before‑consumer ordering.
Task T011 (elemental property loader) depends on T005, yet T005 (base data schemas) is defined later in Phase 2.
Task T012 (descriptor calculator) depends on T010 and T011, both of which are defined after T012 in the document.
Task T013 (composition filter) depends on T012, which appears later, creating a circular ordering problem.
Task T014 (pipeline orchestrator) lists dependencies T008‑T013, many of which are defined after T014, violating deterministic ordering.
US2 tasks (e.g., T016, T017, T018, T020) depend on US1 output T200 (processed descriptor dataset). This makes US2 not independently shippable as required for each user‑story block.
US3 tasks (e.g., T069, T069a, T069b) depend on US2 artifacts such as T018, T021, and T210, breaking the rule that each user‑story’s tasks must form an independently‑shippable unit.

Task T200 is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but writes the central artifact `data/processed/hea_descriptors.csv` that is subsequently consumed by many non‑parallel tasks. While `[P]` only guarantees safety with other `[P]` tasks, the current plan schedules T200 before its consumer tasks, which is correct; however, the `[P]` tag is misleading because the task cannot safely run concurrently with any downstream consumer.
